criteria.criterion: No URL or runtime model fetch
criteria.detail: The traineddata file is located on disk beside the resolved binary (or TESSDATA_PREFIX) and hashed into the manifest; the adapter performs no network I/O of any kind, and the invoked argv contains only the binary, an adapter-generated private temp path, 'stdout' and fixed flags.

Missing binary -> terminal 'unsupported' ('tesseract executable not found'); missing eng.traineddata (nonexistent language) -> terminal 'failed' with 'missing_model: ...'; undecodable raster bytes -> typed 'unreadable_pixels' at open; wall-time overrun -> terminal 'timeout'; a blank but valid raster completes with zero occurrences rather than an error.

criteria.criterion: malicious filename cannot become an option
criteria.detail: Language identifiers are validated against ^[a-z0-9_-]{1,32}$ ('eng --psm 8' is rejected as a terminal unsupported); the crop is saved under the neutral adapter-generated name input.png inside a private mkdtemp directory removed afterwards; the spied invocation argv is exactly [tesseract, <tmp>/input.png, stdout, --psm 3, tsv] with shell=False, so no caller-controlled string reaches the command line.

Padding is max(8 raster px, ceil(10% region height)), clipped at raster edges (corner region never goes negative); CropPlan records the original region, the padded rect and the resize factors with explicit inverse methods; a PSM 7 single-line crop of the F01 render reads '$100' at 0.97 confidence and its TSV box maps back into the original region's canonical footprint; resize (2,2) inverse exactly halves reported boxes.

criteria.criterion: native OCR retains raw punctuation and all occurrences.
criteria.detail: Word TSV rows become one occurrence each with verbatim raw text: case ('SYNTHETIC'), trailing punctuation ('transaction.'), and engine misreads on the F03 bitmap print ('#166,' for '$100.00') are retained, never corrected; word confidence is emitted as a diagnostic EngineScore, not a quality verdict; empty OCR is a completed check with zero occurrences.

environment.engines: tesseract 5.5.3 (leptonica-1.87.0, /opt/homebrew), pypdfium2 5.8.0 renders, Pillow 12.3.0 crops; local eng.traineddata SHA-256 recorded in the manifest
environment.note: OCR runs use the locally installed Tesseract only; no model download, no network access.

limitations: Printed English only, per the capability matrix; non-Latin script OCR support is explicitly not claimed (F14 families stay with native text readers).

The F03 bitmap print OCRs imperfectly by design ('2026-0417' reads as '2626-6417'); the tests assert raw retention and pixel-only behavior, not recognition accuracy. Accuracy targets belong to the alignment/quality tasks (T12, T42).

F15 (OCR material ambiguity) and F20 (worker faults) remain catalog 'specified': the fault-injection mechanics belong to the T29 supervisor; the adapter's typed failure terminals are exercised with timeout/missing-model cases here.
Wall-time kill here terminates the tesseract child only; process-group supervision and partial-result atomicity are T29 scope.
dependency_requests: Fixture owner lane: generate committed F14/F15 families when their recipes are assigned; the adapter consumes any named-render raster, so no adapter change is expected.

measured_decisions.decision: Native full-page default PSM 3 (tesseract automatic), not the browser contract's PSM 6
measured_decisions.reason: Measured on the F01 render: PSM 6 (uniform block) drops the isolated '$100' amount line, while PSM 3 and 11 find it. The Tesseract.js PSM 6 prescription addresses the browser worker path; the native adapter records its PSM per invocation and uses PSM 7 for deliberate single-line user regions, as the contract requires.
measured_decisions.tradeoff: PSM choice is recorded on occurrences (raw_source_locator psm tag) so readings remain comparable across configurations.
measured_decisions.linux_observation_2026_09_12: Spot-check on Linux amd64 tesseract 5.5.3 (artifacts/tasks/T27/psm6-spotcheck.log) shows PSM 6, 3 and 11 all read the identical 16-word sequence including '$100' on the same F01 render: the Mac measurement above does not reproduce on Linux. Default left at PSM 3; contract decision escalated to the coordinator.

measured_decisions.decision: Geometry maps TSV word boxes to canonical points only when the caller records the named-render scale
measured_decisions.reason: COORDINATES.md makes the raster transform chain explicit (O then raster scale); without recorded scale metadata the adapter refuses to guess and emits 'unknown' geometry with null polygon while retaining the raw text (I04, 'raw text is preserved even where geometry is absent').

Runs the full native/tests suite; exit 1 comes solely from the same 5 T26 PDFium geometry baseline failures (72 passed). No T27 OCR failure.

Environment finding, not a T27 finding: 6 failures + 11 errors, ALL in tests/coordination/test_homebase_relay.py, all caused by the relay's intentional canonical-clone guard when the suite runs from a linked task worktree (coordination.canonical_root() resolves git --git-common-dir to the main repo, tripping 'Relay cannot run in a linked worktree'). These relay tests arrived with the merged main and predate no branch work. Counter-evidence: the same relay suite passes 19/19 (+10 subtests) from the canonical Homebase checkout, which stayed clean. Reproducer: run 'git rev-parse --git-common-dir' in a linked worktree (absolute path) vs a plain clone ('.git'). Escalated to the coordinator; scripts/ and tests/coordination/ are reserved paths, not touched.

Real F01 fixture render (public/mapping-amount.pdf, scale 3, 1560x1200px) through the adapter at full-page PSM 3, 6 and 11. Linux tesseract 5.5.3 returns identical 16-word sequences including '$100' for ALL three PSMs: the Mac-based measured rationale that PSM 6 drops the isolated '$100' line does NOT reproduce on Linux amd64.

findings: T26 PDFium geometry tests fail on Linux amd64 exactly as the stopped devin-cloud review recorded (e.g. 1346.400146 != 1365.6); platform drift, T46 parity scope, baseline preserved without weakening tests.
bun run verify fails only in linked task worktrees because the relay guard is environment-sensitive; passes in the canonical checkout. Coordination-owner finding, reserved paths untouched.

PSM-6 spot-check contradicts the Mac measured decision on Linux (PSM 6 finds '$100'); DEFAULT_PSM=3 left unchanged pending Astra's acceptance decision, since the deviation's justification is now platform-dependent.

The partial review's low-sev observation (missing TESSDATA_PREFIX -> PATH-symlinked binary misses tessdata) does not reproduce in the current environment: /usr/sbin/tesseract resolves ../share/tessdata = /usr/share/tessdata and the suite passes 20/20 both with and without TESSDATA_PREFIX set; the local model hash test passes in both runs.
